# Room Tools

This package provides `ui-control-panel` for Node-RED and MUSE Automator.

## ControlPanel

The page author writes ordinary HTML/CSS/Vue and pastes it into the `ui-control-panel` Template. After configuring a Dashboard page, room ID, control login, and separate editor login, save and Deploy. Reopen the node and select **Open binding editor**. Sign in with the editor account, right-click a supported control, choose its device points, and Apply. **Open page** opens the normal control page with its separate user login.

Both logins work over HTTP on a trusted local network. HTTPS is recommended for other networks because HTTP transmits credentials without encryption. Session cookies are marked `Secure` when the connection uses HTTPS.

Bindings are stored in `visualBindings` on the node. The runtime reads that mapping to authenticate commands, route feedback, and generate a native bridge. The page author does not put device paths, `data-cp-*` attributes, or device-send code in the Template. Author-provided `data-cp-*` attributes are rejected.

Supported controls include native range, checkbox, semantic pressed button, select, text input, meter, progress, and simple text display. Give repeated controls distinct standard IDs. Simple top-level Vue `v-model` works, including object-list models such as `item.volume`, `item.audio.volume`, or `items[index].volume`, primitive array models such as `values[index]`, and an inner `<template v-for>` for multiple controls per row. During Vue re-rendering, a temporary duplicate list key is ignored until the key becomes unique again, so bindings do not attach twice. Controls with existing send handlers or ambiguous dynamic behavior are rejected until a suitable adapter exists. See `CONTROL_PANEL_AI_GUIDE.md` for examples and limits.

Native semantic buttons support a binding-editor **Button behavior** setting: **Click to toggle** (the default for existing bindings) or **Hold to activate**. Momentary buttons require `both` mode, send boolean true on press and false on release, and always display real device feedback rather than a predicted local state. Pointer cancellation, keyboard release, focus/visibility loss, DOM removal, and disconnect release the hold. A 3-second server lease attempts release if the browser disappears; lease renewal does not repeat device writes. Concurrent holders of the same Write point within one panel are combined until the last release. Other panels and external controllers are not coordinated. Device or bridge outages can prevent physical release, so feedback remains the authority. Drivers keep the existing boolean Toggle contract; page authors do not implement hold events or lease traffic.

Writable native semantic buttons in either behavior automatically show a separate physical press effect (2px downward translation and inset shadow) for pointer/touch and Space/Enter. Release, cancellation, focus/visibility loss, disablement, DOM removal and loss of the authenticated feedback connection clear it. This effect changes neither the Vue model nor device-feedback ARIA, colors or icons; device feedback remains the sole source of the indicated mute/power state. Read-only buttons and editor mode do not show this effect. Page authors need no extra event handlers or internal press attributes.

Realtime meter delivery does not change the page-authoring contract. Authors use ordinary `meter`, `progress`, `v-progress-linear`, or `v-progress-circular` controls with stable IDs and simple top-level fields. They do not declare devices, point paths, stream IDs, sockets, subscriptions, or frame formats. A `volume` binding is a writable gain setting with ordinary feedback; a `meter` binding is read-only realtime signal telemetry and requires a target that advertises Meter metadata. A normal numeric `level` target is not automatically a Meter. When the selected feedback point advertises realtime meter delivery, ControlPanel automatically shares the device stream, projects complete frames to the bound controls, applies webpage-side range conversion, and handles stale/reconnected data.

Readonly XY-series telemetry follows the same page boundary. Use a standard canvas with one simple Vue array binding, for example `<canvas id="spectrum" :data-points="spectrum"></canvas>`, or a map container with `<div id="room-map" :data-coordinates="locations"></div>`. Map coordinates use the standard `[longitude, latitude]` order. The page receives complete `[[x, y], ...]` snapshots; ControlPanel owns subscription, latest-frame replacement, stale handling, and reconnection. The page does not declare a device, stream, socket, or frame protocol. XY-series is independent from Meter and Volume: it never sends commands and does not represent a single scalar value.

Different XY-series streams arrive independently. Room delivery aggregates their latest snapshots, not synchronized samples from a shared acquisition frame. The public framework defaults to 2048 points per stream and allows a configured maximum of 8192; the receiver enforces the manifest's `maxPoints`. A panel supports at most 256 XY-series bindings. These limits do not guarantee throughput at every frame rate or concurrency level; validate performance in the target environment.

Vuetify adapters cover `v-slider`, `v-switch`, `v-checkbox`, `v-select`, `v-radio-group`, `v-text-field`, `v-textarea`, and read-only `v-progress-linear` and `v-progress-circular`. Interactive components use a simple top-level `v-model`; progress may also use a simple `:model-value` field. Sliders accept fixed numeric `min`, `max`, and `step` props, including numeric Vue bindings such as `:max="100"`. Text fields commit on change, blur, or Enter (`v-text-field` only). Selection values must match the device's enum values; circular progress uses a fixed 0-100 range. `v-model.number` is accepted for numeric sliders and scalar selections, but not for boolean or text controls. Dynamic bounds, array-valued switches, multi-select, object selections, custom true/false values, indeterminate progress, and controls with their own event handlers need a separate adapter.

Use paired Vuetify tags in Dashboard templates, such as `<v-slider></v-slider>`; self-closing component tags can absorb the following controls during Dashboard rendering and are rejected before deployment.

After clicking Apply in the page binding editor, the package validates the mapping, backs up the active Flow, and generates the native bridge for that panel using the original 1.8.9 flow. Apply does not click Deploy for the user. When Automator reports the external Flow change, the editor refreshes its Flow view once; review the refreshed Flow and deploy it yourself. The bridge revision must match the saved mapping before a command can reach a device. A Node-RED simulation verifies software behavior, while live device operation requires a separate check.

The current runtime has one panel-scoped control path. The retired topic-based region gateway, fixed demo scenes, hand-written control tags, and `sendControl` authoring API are not supported. The page editor and server use the same target compatibility rules.

## Installation

Install this package in the Node-RED user directory or declare it in the active project `package.json`. Installing on the Mac does not install the package on a MUSE controller.

The binding editor uses the running Node-RED server's loopback port and admin root to read the AMX device catalog, on both desktop Automator and MUSE. No desktop-only catalog environment variable is required. The AMX catalog routes must be available on that runtime.

Node.js 18.16.0 or newer is required. Dashboard 2 and the AMX Command/Status/Event nodes must be installed separately. The active Node-RED project must declare its Flow and credentials filenames; its user directory must be writable for private backups. Authenticated LAN users can Apply; Flow administration itself stays on loopback. Direct TLS or an authenticated Node-RED admin API needs an additional server-side transport adapter and is not configured automatically.

The release includes `npm-shrinkwrap.json` to install the tested dependency versions. Deploy/Push must reference the intended registry version or a controller-accessible tarball; a `file:` dependency pointing at a Mac path is not portable to MUSE. Restart the controller runtime after replacing module code.

For development, run `node --test test-*.cjs`. The isolated integration test uses the executing Node version; `CP_TEST_NODE` and `CP_TEST_PANEL_PACKAGE` can select an alternate runtime and unpacked release package.
